transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-19
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Samira Holt (Redwood AE), Miguel Ortega (Redwood SE), Jenna Park (Redwood Solutions), Priya Natarajan (LingualHealth Platform Eng), Daniel Park (SRE Lead), Evelyn Zhao (Head of Trust), Marco Ruiz (Backend)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be noisy):
- Walkthrough of Console request tracing, error analysis workflow, and request logs.
- Demo of trace playback, KV-cache considerations, and fallback routing.
- Discussed hosted vs dedicated for privacy and latency; customer concerned about PII and KMS integration.
- Agreed to run a short POC: 24h capture + replay with KV cache toggled and an analysis report.

Topics: request tracing, request-forensics, KV cache, fallback policies, PII/KMS, dedicated capacity POC, trace sampling

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samira: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samira from Redwood, AE on this account. Miguel is our SE who will drive the console demo and the trace playbook. Jenna's here to jump in on questions about integrations.
[00:12] Priya: Hey thanks, Priya here. We're most interested in the debugging flow — how we can quickly go from an error in prod to root cause, and what data is retained.
[00:20] Miguel: Great, that is exactly what we'll show. Quick agenda: show the live trace inspector, playback a failing request, inspect KV cache interactions, and then show fallback routing to cheaper model variants. We'll also cover security controls (KMS, RBAC).
[00:34] Daniel: Cool. Our constraints: HIPAA-adjacent data, so we need private deployment or at least customer-managed KMS. Latency SLO is 200ms p95 for short prompts and we have bursts during clinic hours.
[00:48] Samira: Understood. We'll show how Dedicated vs Hosted maps to that. For footprints with PII we usually recommend private or Dedicated with customer KMS, but we'll show encryption options now.
[01:05] Miguel: Jumping into the console — bear with me, audio is a bit fuzzy, I might say KV "cash" — that's the transcriber again, but it's KV cache, right.
[01:17] Jenna: (laughs) noted.
[01:20] Miguel: Ok I'm on the Requests tab. You can see recent requests with colored state: succeeded, degraded, errored. I'll filter to errored in the last 24 hours.
[01:33] [screen share noise]
[01:36] Miguel: Here's an example request where the model timed out after fallback to a smaller variant. We capture the entire trace: incoming headers, routing decision (hosted vs dedicated), model variant, token counts, and the KV cache hit/miss timeline.
[01:53] Priya: How long do you keep the full payloads by default? We need to ensure PHI is not retained longer than our policy.
[01:59] Miguel: Default retention on hosted is 30 days for full traces, with redaction options. For Dedicated/Private you can configure retention and disable storing full prompt discards; we also integrate with customer KMS if you want envelope encryption.
[02:12] Evelyn: Do you support on-prem key stores or only cloud KMS?
[02:16] Miguel: We support cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS), and HSM via customer-managed key adapters in Private deployments — it's in the security whitepaper I'll share.
[02:25] Daniel: You mentioned KV cache impacts. What's the recommended workflow when investigating hallucinations or stale context?
[02:31] Miguel: Good question. When a user sees stale content, first check KV cache hit rate in the trace. We show a KV timeline with operations — gets/sets — and you can toggle to replay the request with KV cache disabled. That lets you see if the cache influenced token selection. For POC we often replay with KV off, and then with quantization variants to compare outputs.
[02:50] Marco: Is replay exact? Like do you re-run on same hardware, same random seed?
[02:54] Miguel: We replay against the same model version pinned in the trace. We can't guarantee identical GPU nondeterminism (sampling) unless you pin deterministic decode params — but for troubleshooting we recommend deterministic sampling (top_k=1 or temperature=0) to reproduce. We also snapshot the model version and quantization profile used.
[03:14] Priya: Can you show the playback UI?
[03:18] Miguel: Sure — playing back now. You can scrub through the token stream or watch a condensed step timeline. At each token step you can see the KV read/writes. Here I fast-forward to the error: you can see a large spike in latency at token 42, and then the fallback policy triggered to model-compact-v1.
[03:36] [short pause, clicks]
[03:40] Miguel: The error detail is an upstream network timeout to the worker host. The trace links to infra logs and the GPU host metrics in a side panel.
[03:48] Daniel: That's helpful. We have autoscaling events correlated with high inbound load. Does the console show which route took the request?
[03:55] Miguel: Yes — the routing decision is shown with reasons: e.g., "region mismatch" or "capacity constraint". You can simulate conditions via the routing simulator to test fallback behavior.
[04:08] Priya: About logs, can we stream them into our ELK or Splunk?
[04:12] Samira: Yes, you can push exports or use our webhook sink to send traces to your observability pipeline; for Dedicated we also offer direct log-forwarding connectors.
[04:22] Evelyn: On compliance, does Redwood provide audit trails for access to traces? We need tamper-evident logs.
[04:28] Miguel: Audit logs are available; each trace access event is recorded. In Private deployments you can ship audit logs to your SIEM; we surface an immutable event hash for tamper-evidence.
[04:40] Priya: Great. Another practical question: our SREs often need a quick way to triage — is there a checklist?
[04:46] Miguel: We have a Debug Playbook built into the console: Step 1: filter errored requests, Step 2: group by model rollouts, Step 3: inspect KV hit/miss, Step 4: run a replay with deterministic decoding, Step 5: if still failing, escalate to fallback policy review and open a support trace. I'll open the playbook now.
[05:05] [screen share: playbook steps visible]
[05:09] Miguel: You can create a "triage template" per team. It attaches a standard set of logs and a permalink to the trace in the support ticket.
[05:18] Daniel: How do we test worst-case latency? Can we simulate production bursts?
[05:22] Miguel: We have a synthetic load tool that can run through the API with real token distributions. For Dedicated we can schedule burst capacity or reserve a buffer. The console will show p50/p95/p99 histograms and trace samples for the high percentiles.
[05:38] Priya: Ok, switching topics: do you support redaction on ingest for PII?
[05:42] Jenna: Yes, we support on-ingest redaction rules with regex and nlp-based scrubbers; you can mask or hash fields before they're stored. For Private setups we recommend scrubbing at the edge before sending.
[05:53] Marco: What about cost — replaying many requests seems heavy. Any throttles?
[05:57] Samira: Replays are metered, and for POC we include a modest replay allotment. For large-scale replaying we recommend sampling the most suspicious traces. Our Optimize tool can suggest optimal sample sizes to balance cost and triage coverage.
[06:12] Priya: Could you show an example where the playbook detected a regression between two model versions?
[06:16] Miguel: Sure — here's a diff view. We take two pinned model versions and compare generation distributions and token-level logits. You can see this run where model-v2.1 had a higher entropy and produced more off-topic responses; the console flagged it and suggested quantization profile adjustments.
[06:36] Daniel: That level of detail is good. For our legal team, we need to know who accessed which traces around a particular patient request.
[06:44] Miguel: You can query audit logs for trace id and filter by user/email and action type. The trace view also lists the last 10 accesses.
[06:52] Evelyn: On the POC, we'd likely need Dedicated given PHI — do we need a long lead time for that?
[06:58] Samira: Depends on region and GPU availability. Standard Dedicated setup usually takes 2-3 weeks; Private (on-prem) is longer. For the immediate POC we can do a Dedicated eval with a short-term reserved pool.
[07:10] [small cross-talk]
[07:13] Priya: What about data residency? Some of our clinics are in EU and require EU data residency.
[07:18] Miguel: We have EU regions and routing policies to pin requests to EU-hosted capacity; for Private you can fully localize control plane.
[07:26] Daniel: Let's do a practical troubleshooting scenario. Here's an example: POST body with repeated instruction, users seeing inconsistent completions across requests.
[07:32] Priya: I'll paste the sample request we sent earlier.
[07:36] [paste noise]
[07:38] Miguel: Ok loading it into the replay tool. First, I'll run with the same model pinned and default sampling. You can see slight differences due to sampling. Now toggling deterministic params — response is reproducible. Next toggle KV cache: with cache enabled the response contains an older snippet; with cache off the fresh prompt is used.
[07:59] Marco: So the cache had stale keys. How do we invalidate?
[08:02] Miguel: You can set TTLs for KV keys, or evict on write. We also show a "cache entries" explorer so you can inspect specific keys and invalidate.
[08:12] Priya: Are KV keys stored with any PII? We try not to persist patient identifiers.
[08:17] Jenna: Keys are customer-managed; you can choose to hash keys or exclude certain fields before storage. That's configurable per route.
[08:25] Daniel: If we wanted to run the 24h capture POC, what do you need from us?
[08:29] Samira: We'll need a sample dataset, a list of routes to capture, and the retention rules (redact or store). We'll set up a dedicated test pool with replay capability. Miguel, can you note the steps?
[08:37] Miguel: Yup. Step A: create test routes and tokens; Step B: enable high-fidelity tracing for 24h; Step C: export traces to S3 or your SIEM; Step D: run replay and deliver report. I'll attach the runbook after the call.
[08:50] Priya: That works. A couple more minor things — how easy is it to onboard Platform engineers? We need self-serve docs.
[08:56] Jenna: We have an onboarding repo with example cURLs, SDK snippets, and a quickstart for trace sampling. I'll share the link.
[09:04] [pause]
[09:06] Daniel: Any gotchas we should know about?
[09:08] Miguel: Watch out for high sampling rates in prod — it increases egress and storage. Use stratified sampling: high sampling on errors and low sampling on success. Also be careful with replaying PII — redact where possible or use ephemeral keys.
[09:24] Priya: Ok, from a timeline perspective, we want to evaluate this week and run the POC next.
[09:30] Samira: Sounds good. We'll aim to send the security packet and the runbook today, and target 10/26 for starting the 24h capture.
[09:38] Marco: One last technical: can we run the replay against a canary model in our VPC?
[09:43] Miguel: For Dedicated yes. For Hosted, we can route to a canary variant in the same region; for Private we can deploy a canary in your VPC. We also have isolation controls for canary traffic.
[09:56] Evelyn: Thanks for walking through everything. This was helpful.
[10:00] Samira: Great, we'll follow up. I'll summarize next steps.
